unit.why: A short ethical teaching on closing shops early before Shabbat, framing an exemplary tale about R. Isserl, father of the Rema, a pre-Hasidic figure.

stories.start_quote: ושמעתי מעשה נפלא מהגביר ר׳ איסורל
stories.end_quote: רבינו הרמ״א [א״ה הנני נכדו] מאורן של ישראל
stories.summary_en: Samael, disguised as a great nobleman, tries to keep the silk merchant R. Isserl trading past midday on Friday. Isserl closes his shop anyway, losing a large sale, and Heaven rewards him with a holy son, the Rema.

tags.why: The whole tale turns on closing the shop early on Sabbath eve.

tags.why: Samael acts as the tempter (the 'ba'al davar').
